content:
Tiago Ferrão-Lindqvist
Data Engineering | Test & Validation Engineering

Setúbal, Portugal | tiago.ferraolindqvist@example.com | +351 555 010 311
linkedin.com/in/tfl-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation, and practical data tooling. Develops Python scripts to process test-rig data, check results against specifications and generate reports, including a nightly tool used by four test engineers. Experienced querying SQL Server test data and building Power BI dashboards for engineering users. Currently developing data engineering knowledge through an online course and personal projects.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Test & Validation Engineer | Corvane Automotive Components | Setúbal
Mar 2019–Present
- Plan and run durability, vibration and climatic tests on seat-adjuster mechanisms across six servo-hydraulic and electric test rigs; prepare test reports for OEM customers.
- Develop Python scripts using pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib and npTDMS to process TDMS and CSV rig files, flag channels outside test specifications and generate report figures. The tool processes approximately 2 GB of data per week and reduced report preparation from about three days to half a day per test.
- Run the reporting tool nightly on a lab PC using Windows Task Scheduler. It writes summary results to an IT-provisioned staging table in the plant’s SQL Server database and is used by four other test engineers.
- Query test results in SQL Server for trend analysis across three product generations.
- Built a Power BI dashboard using the staging table to show pass/fail trends and cycles to failure by product generation; used by about 15 validation and design engineers.
- Correlate test-rig results with FEA in ANSYS Mechanical and lead 8D root-cause analysis on field failures. Proposed a redesigned adjuster rail bracket that reduced warranty returns for that part by 40%.
- Maintain MATLAB/Simulink models of the adjuster drive used to select rig load profiles that match customer duty cycles.
- Trained three apprentices in rig safety and test setup (2022–2024).

Mechanical Design Engineer | Halvik Pumps | Porto
Sep 2014–Feb 2019
- Designed industrial centrifugal-pump casings and impellers in SolidWorks and prepared production drawings with GD&T; owned DFMEA for two product lines.
- Performed structural FEA of pump casings in ANSYS. Supported the change of one casing family from grey cast iron to ductile iron, saving 12% in material cost.
- Supported conversion of the pump performance test bench to a PLC-controlled setup, including changes to setpoints and timers in Siemens TIA Portal alongside the automation engineer.
- Wrote a LabVIEW data-acquisition program for the performance test bench, reducing test setup time from about two hours to 30 minutes.

SELECTED DATA PROJECTS

Bike-sharing Trips API | Personal Learning Project | 2025
- Built a small Flask API over a public bike-sharing dataset loaded into SQLite, with three read-only endpoints.
- Followed a tutorial to run the project using Docker Compose; maintained personal repositories with Git.

Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool | Corvane Automotive Components | 2021–Present
- Built Python scripts to parse test-rig output, validate channels against test specifications and generate standard report figures.
- Technologies: Python, pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS, SQL Server, Windows Task Scheduler.

Test Results Dashboard | Corvane Automotive Components | 2023
- Created a Power BI dashboard showing pass/fail trends and cycles to failure per product generation for validation and design engineers.
- Technologies: Power BI, SQL.

Adjuster Drive Load-Profile Model | Corvane Automotive Components | 2020–Present
- Maintains a MATLAB/Simulink model of the seat-adjuster drive, including motor, gearbox and rail friction, to help select rig load profiles.
- Technologies: MATLAB, Simulink.

EDUCATION
MSc Mechanical Engineering | Sado Valley Polytechnic | 2014
Thesis: Fatigue life prediction of welded brackets under variable-amplitude loading

PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
Online Data Engineering Course | In progress
Completed 6 of 9 modules.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Data and programming: Python (pandas, NumPy, Matplotlib, npTDMS), SQL, MATLAB/Simulink, Flask, SQLite, Excel/VBA
Data reporting and analysis: Power BI, LabVIEW, Minitab, design of experiments (DOE)
Engineering: ANSYS Mechanical, SolidWorks, CATIA V5, GD&T, DFMEA, 8D problem solving
Tools: Git (personal projects), Docker Compose (personal learning project), Windows Task Scheduler

LANGUAGES
Portuguese (native) | English (fluent) | Spanish (good)

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, professional, and unusually specific about engineering-data work. Strong quantified evidence includes processing approximately 2 GB of data per week, reducing reporting time from three days to half a day, supporting four test engineers, and providing a dashboard used by about 15 engineers. The progression from mechanical engineering and validation into practical data tooling is credible and easy to understand. The document also distinguishes employment experience from personal learning projects and accurately presents the in-progress data-engineering course. Its main limitation is not writing quality but the substantial distance between the candidate's current experience and a senior data-platform role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, conventional reverse-chronological structure, readable bullets, and no tables, graphics, text boxes, or complex formatting that would commonly impair ATS parsing. It includes relevant terms such as Python, SQL Server, data processing, Power BI, Docker Compose, Git, SQLite, data validation, and Windows Task Scheduler. However, the document does not contain evidence for core platform keywords such as Google Cloud, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Airflow, dbt, CI/CD, cloud data warehouse, data modelling, or query optimisation. These are genuine experience gaps rather than keywords that should be inserted. The strong metrics and explicit technologies improve the likelihood of human review, but automated screening for a senior data-platform position may still rank the CV low because several mandatory stack and platform terms are absent.
critique.job_alignment_feedback:
The document shows strong transferable experience in engineering data processing, automated reporting, data-quality checks against specifications, SQL Server querying, dashboard development, and practical ownership of an internal tool used by multiple engineers. It also shows professional English and Portuguese, and it provides credible evidence of curiosity through an online data-engineering course, personal projects, Docker Compose, Git, and a Flask API. The candidate's engineering background may also support collaboration with technical and BI users, although the CV does not explicitly describe work with data scientists or analytics engineers.

The candidate's material shows gaps in designing, building, and operating production data platforms or cloud data warehouses at scale; advanced Python and SQL with query optimisation on large datasets; strong data modelling; hands-on Google Cloud or comparable cloud experience; and graph modelling. The candidate has no stated experience with GCP, BigQuery, Cloud Run, GKE, Airflow, dbt, Spark, Kafka, CI/CD, or production cloud deployment. The document should not imply those capabilities. The role is therefore a stretch for the advertised senior level, but the CV presents a truthful and reasonably compelling adjacent profile for a junior or mid-level data-engineering opportunity.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence, "Currently developing data engineering knowledge through an online course and personal projects," with a more evidence-based version such as: "Currently developing data-engineering knowledge through an online course and personal projects, including a Flask API backed by SQLite and Docker Compose." This makes the learning evidence more concrete without implying production cloud experience.

2. In the Professional Summary, change "practical data tooling" to "engineering data tooling and automated reporting" and add the supported outcome that the tool is used by four test engineers. For example: "Mechanical engineer with 12 years of experience in product design, testing and validation, and engineering data tooling. Develops Python scripts to validate test-rig data, generate reports, and support engineering decisions; a nightly internal tool is used by four test engineers." This improves alignment with reusable tooling and data-quality work while remaining truthful.

3. In the Rig Data Processing and Reporting Tool project, make the data-quality aspect more explicit by changing "flag channels outside the test specifications" to "perform data-quality checks by flagging channels outside test specifications." This uses relevant terminology supported by the work and helps ATS matching without claiming formal enterprise data-governance experience.

4. In the Technical Skills section, change "SQL" to "SQL Server SQL (read-only querying and reporting)" or "SQL Server (read-only querying)" to accurately define the level and context of database experience. Retain the existing project bullet explaining that the staging table was IT-provisioned; this prevents recruiters from interpreting the experience as database or platform ownership.

Advanced Python and SQL, including query optimisation on large datasets
Hands-on experience with Google Cloud or a comparable cloud
Curiosity about new data architecture ideas and open-source practices
